    Integrate existing runtime features for the production recovery (#40)
    
    * Model a relation as entity data, with the address kept out of it
    
    relations.validatedContacts.<id> already holds, fail-closed, how to
    reach a person. EntityRelationRecordV1 adds relations.records.<id> for
    everything else the tie is: where it came from and when, what the
    person does in which of my contexts, declared and inferred interests
    apart, channels as opaque refs, standing, evidence of contact as
    references to credentials, and a running interaction summary. The
    validator refuses any channel ref that reads as an address, so the
    record can follow the entity to another surface without becoming a
    contact list on the way.
    
    Interactions are chronicle entries, chronicle[id=relation-event-…],
    bound to their relation at the keypath; the record keeps only the sum.
    applying(_:chronicleRef:) is pure so the summary can be tested without
    a store. A metadata-mode event drops its summary in the initialiser
    and is refused by the validator if one is smuggled in afterwards.
    
    EntityRelationReachPlanner turns a record into «how do I start a
    conversation with this person»: chat if they have an entity,
    correspondence if the channel exists, nearby while it is fresh, else an
    invitation on the address we hold. A resend inside seven days is named
    as one. Pure and deterministic, so the app, the butler and the scaffold
    give the same answer for the same person.
    
    EntityAnchorCell admits the namespace through the batch path only,
    rejects direct writes to it, and serves the value-free schema at
    entityRelationSchema.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0166zoWBapoQ3R6iiJrhd2xx
    
    * Refuse to become the owner's vault before the owner has authenticated
    
    A dismissed Face ID sheet returned from initialize() exactly like a
    successful one. Callers then made IdentityVault the default vault, asked
    it for the "private" identity, and got a freshly minted one with no key
    material behind it — so every identity-unique cell failed owner
    validation and the app told Kjetil, truthfully but uselessly, that the
    local HAVEN cells could not be validated. authenticatedRuntimeIsReady
    agreed everything was fine, because it only checked the vault's type.
    
    isAuthenticated is now the honest answer, set only after the owner
    authenticated and the identities loaded. authenticatev2 throws when the
    passcode fallback returns false or no policy can be evaluated, instead
    of returning as though nothing happened. AppInitializer keeps whatever
    vault is active until isAuthenticated says otherwise.
    
    EntityScanner becomes identityUnique. Scaffold-unique meant one instance
    owned by whichever identity happened to create it, and every other
    identity — the verifier's, the authenticated one after Face ID — was
    denied encounters and radar outright. Only one identity drives local
    surfaces at a time, so nothing is actually shared by making the
    scanner's encounters belong to their owner.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0166zoWBapoQ3R6iiJrhd2xx
    
    * Draw the nearby scanner as a radar instead of a stack of blocks
    
    The scanner surface listed its findings. A list is the wrong shape for
    "who is near me, and how near": distance and bearing are the whole
    point, and they were text.
    
    RadarEntityLedger folds the scanner's flow events into one current
    picture — pure value semantics, so the view model on a screen and the
    cell that emits the events hold the same picture, and the cell can hand
    it to a skeleton without a view model in between. RadarViewModel now
    delegates to it rather than keeping a second copy.
    
    Visualization(kind: "radar") draws that picture: range rings with metres
    on them, a sweep while scanning, blips that burn when just heard and
    fade as they go quiet, and the nearest distance as one large number.
    A bearing we do not have is drawn as a dashed arc at the right radius,
    never as a confident dot somewhere — a guessed angle must not look
    measured. Tapping a blip writes scanner.select. The radar polls once a
    second while on screen; every other visualization still refreshes on
    mutation only, as before.
    
    EntityScannerCell serves that spec at `radar` and takes the selection
    at `select`, so a surface gets the whole thing from two keypaths.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0166zoWBapoQ3R6iiJrhd2xx
    
    * Report the parts of a skeleton the person will never see
    
    A visibility condition that cannot be resolved evaluates to false, which is
    indistinguishable from one that is legitimately not met. So an element gated
    on data the renderer does not have at that position never appears, nothing
    reports it, and the surface looks finished while doing nothing.
    
    That is not hypothetical. HAVEN's Relations workbench shipped with seven
    root-level sections gated on `relations.state…`, `contactImport.state…` and
    `invitation.state…`. At root the renderer passes no value — SkeletonView
    defaults userInfoValue to nil — so every gate was false and the owner got a
    title over an empty card. Twelve actions were unreachable, among them
    picking a file and committing an import. Every existing test was green,
    because every existing test reads through porthole.get, and that is not the
    path the renderer uses to decide visibility.
    
    SkeletonReachabilityAudit answers the question a schema check cannot: will
    anyone ever see this. It decides by calling the renderer's own condition
    evaluation with the renderer's own root inputs, so it cannot drift from what
    the screen does. Scope carries the whole argument: at root nothing resolves,
    while inside a List/Grid/Reference row the row's value is passed down, so
    conditions there are answerable at runtime and are left alone.
    
    Findings name what the owner loses, not that a node is hidden —
    `lostActionKeypaths` is what turns a structural finding into a purpose
    finding. reachableActionKeypaths gives the other half: the set an
    expectation contract can be checked against, so "the owner can import a
    file" becomes something a test can hold.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0166zoWBapoQ3R6iiJrhd2xx

    Fire kildefiler og kontraktstestene har ligget utracket i arbeidstreet siden
    2. og 7. september. S6 forutsetter en landet revisjon som inneholder dem.
    
    Målt natt til 9. september, mot dette arbeidstreet:
    swift build --build-tests: exit 0
    7 av 7 CorrespondenceCellTests passerer
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019mpvrWDd5nFPfPXaba7tyX

    * fix(bridge): presentert deskriptor gir aldri lokal signeringsvault (HD-0080, WP-S1 bridge-provenance)
    
    * test(bridge): fang peer-avslaget slik BridgeIdentityVault pakker det (HD-0080)
    
    * wip(tillitspakke): land the agent trust package, nearby proofs and node-model work
    
    AgentTrustPackage, EffectReceipt and ReceiptSignature with tests; nearby
    advertisement exchange and proof session; EntityRepresentation/Interest/Purpose
    codec work including nodeIdentifier preservation and EntityRelationPerspective;
    skeleton localization runtime.
    
    Not build-verified. Branch commit only — nothing here reaches main until it is.
    
    * Integrate existing native skeleton layout parity fixes
    
    Port 6218ed591387c7f2899a4441186e4877398def59 and fa7982d7fd5ecb3156ad2e576b9860e2ff3aca51 layout hunks while preserving current dynamic modifiers and localization. The resolver prefetch from 6218ed5 is already integrated.
    
    * Keep private scanner state owner-only and make trust fixtures self-contained
    
    Remove radar/select from restored agreement templates, deny non-owner reads and selections, and keep selection details out of shared flow. Preserve existing agreement surface sentinel. Full regression exposed these gaps; all 23 affected tests now pass.
    
    * Measure the exact candidate in runtime capacity CI
    
    * Synchronize web style parity inventory with integrated surfaces
